mgmt_bio.text: Elliott Hill, 61, became Nike's chief executive in 2024, succeeding John Donahoe, a tech-oriented outsider who had led eBay and ServiceNow before joining Nike in 2020. Hill is a Nike lifer who started as an intern in 1988 and rose to oversee all commercial and marketing operations for both Nike and the Jordan brand, and his appointment was a deliberate move to rebuild a leadership team with deep Nike DNA, meaning executives who know the brand, the product and the wholesale ecosystem. Under his leadership, capital is directed first into the business, mainly demand creation and product innovation and more recently supply chain restructuring and rebuilding wholesale relationships, with excess capital returned via the dividend and opportunistic buybacks rather than acquisitions.
